title: Liquidity and Autocorrelations in Individual Stock Returns
one_line: Short-term (weekly) stock return reversals are concentrated in high-turnover, illiquid stocks — the reversal is a compensation for providing liquidity, not an inefficiency; profits largely vanish after costs.

findings.statement: Reversal strongest among high-turnover, low-liquidity stocks.

reported_results.headline: Short-term (weekly) stock return reversals are concentrated in high-turnover, illiquid stocks — the reversal is a compensation for providing liquidity, not an inefficiency; profits largely vanish after costs.

tradable_edge: Stock-level; supports treating index reversal rules as liquidity premia that need tight cost modelling.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Only the abstract / a secondary summary was reachable (SSRN is blocked from chat sessions); numbers not verified against the full paper.
